units.function: Tests enumerating Secret provider capabilities and diagnosing insecure permissions on the local encrypted provider master-key file.
units.dependencyDirection: Process environment and local filesystem configuration feed a provider registry that returns capability descriptors and health/warning/backup guidance.
units.keyDataModels: Provider ID, managed-value/external-reference support, configured state, health status/warnings/details/backup guidance and master key env/file path/mode.
units.lifecycle: Registry lists local and AWS providers; local provider is immediately configured, while AWS is not. Health checks warn when the local key file is group/world readable and advise mode 0600 plus coordinated database backup.
units.testAssessment: Valuable capability and file-mode checks are covered. Missing are key length/format, owner/symlink/path permissions, environment-key leakage, provider connectivity/auth, external reference resolution, rotation/versioning, revoke/delete, HSM/KMS/Vault adapters, tenant isolation, degraded behavior and redaction of key paths/errors.
units.designRationale: Expose a pluggable secret backend catalog and catch common self-hosted encryption-key operational mistakes.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a replaceable SecretPort supporting managed cloud and enterprise/local vaults with explicit health, lifecycle and data residency.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT provider capability descriptors and structured health checks. Keep provider config deployment-scoped, secret references Company-scoped, immutable versions approval-bound, and add rotation/revocation/export/backup ceremonies, KMS/Vault plugins and path/detail redaction.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configured availability does not prove which administrator owns the key ceremony or that restore/rotation was approved. Diagnostic details expose the key-file path, and ambient environment ownership is not an accountable secret contract.

units.function: Unit policy tests suppressing noisy successful polling/static HTTP access logs while retaining ordinary application successes and all failures.
units.dependencyDirection: HTTP method, raw path/query and status enter a middleware predicate producing a logging decision.
units.keyDataModels: Method/path/status and endpoint categories for health, runs, Issues, activity, badges and static assets.
units.lifecycle: 304, successful poll/static requests are silenced; ordinary API changes/reads and failed requests remain visible.
units.testAssessment: Representative positive/negative routes are covered. Missing are normalized/encoded paths, new endpoints, latency/size sampling, security-sensitive successful reads, query-secret redaction and proof that suppressed access logs are not the only audit evidence.
units.designRationale: Keep operational logs usable under high-frequency UI polling without hiding failures.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs separate operational telemetry and immutable responsibility audit so sampling one cannot erase the other.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the noise policy only; use route metadata rather than raw string patterns, redact before logging, and never apply sampling to approval, identity, permission, data export or responsibility events.
units.responsibilityConflict: Successful activity and Run reads are silenced, so HTTP logs cannot be treated as an access audit. Company OS must have a distinct authorized-access/audit owner where required.

units.function: Unit tests masking the active OS username in paths, standalone text and recursively nested log-event values.
units.dependencyDirection: Configured usernames/home directories and arbitrary strings/objects/arrays enter a log sanitization helper; masked values flow to telemetry.
units.keyDataModels: Username/home paths, deterministic masked username, nested object/array values and enabled flag.
units.lifecycle: Exact path/word-boundary username occurrences are masked across Unix/Windows forms and nested payloads; larger tokens remain unchanged and redaction can be disabled.
units.testAssessment: Useful cross-platform, word-boundary and recursive cases are covered. Missing are cycles, Date/Map/Set/Error/Buffer, symbols/getters, Unicode/case variants, email/URL encoding, arbitrary PII and proof redaction happens before every sink. A disable flag is risky in production.
units.designRationale: Reduce accidental developer/operator identity leakage from local paths without destroying unrelated strings.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS logs/evidence require layered secret/PII classification and tenant policy, not only current username masking.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the sink-boundary recursive sanitizer as one PII rule; use schema-aware classifications, cycle-safe traversal, non-disableable production baselines and explicit original-evidence storage policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Masking a username can also remove attribution needed for evidence; audit records should retain opaque Principal IDs while presentation logs redact OS identities.

units.function: Tests for a release-time repository scanner combining OS usernames and a custom forbidden-token file, invoking text search and blocking publication on matches.
units.dependencyDirection: Environment/userInfo and an optional plaintext token list produce search terms; an injected command scans the repository and matched output is written to CI error logs.
units.keyDataModels: Dynamic/file token list, repository root, search output, exit code and build-block message.
units.lifecycle: Usernames are deduplicated, resolution failures degrade to no dynamic tokens, file terms merge in, every token is searched and any match blocks the build while printing matching lines.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover environment fallback, merge/deduplication and multi-token scanning. The claimed non-leak property checks only that token names are not separately labeled; real search output generally includes the matching source line and therefore the forbidden secret itself. Missing are fingerprints/redacted findings, binary/generated/history scanning, entropy/pattern detectors, false positives, command argument safety, large token sets and incident rotation workflow.
units.designRationale: Prevent machine/user-specific or sensitive literals from entering published source artifacts.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs source and artifact secret scanning that never republishes discovered credentials into CI logs.
units.companyOsFit: Reject this implementation for secrets. Use a maintained secret scanner with fingerprints and redacted file/line findings, scan history/build artifacts/dependencies, protect scanner inputs as secrets, and trigger revoke/rotate/quarantine workflow. A separate non-secret portability-token check may reuse the simple concept.
units.responsibilityConflict: The blocker can leak the very token it detects through matched source lines, expanding incident exposure. It also provides no owner, revocation status or remediation evidence.

units.function: Unit tests parsing typed SecretRef binding objects and collecting nested secret-ref fields from JSON Schema properties/composition.
units.dependencyDirection: Untrusted config values and adapter/plugin JSON Schemas enter helpers that normalize SecretRef identity/version and derive dot paths for later secret handling.
units.keyDataModels: secret_ref type, UUID secretId, latest or positive numeric version, JSON Schema properties/allOf/oneOf and dot path.
units.lifecycle: Valid binding objects parse with latest default or a pinned numeric version; raw strings, invalid UUID/type/version and arrays are rejected. Schema traversal finds nested direct and composed secret-ref formats.
units.testAssessment: Strong basic shape rejection and composition cases are covered. Missing are anyOf/if-then-else/$ref/arrays/additionalProperties/patternProperties, cycles, escaped property names, schema depth limits, provider/Company ownership and authorization. Defaulting to latest is unsafe for approval-bound execution.
units.designRationale: Let plugin/adapter configuration remain JSON-shaped while marking fields that resolve through centralized secret storage.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector SDK schemas need typed secret handles without permitting raw credentials or mutable approval drift.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT typed binding and schema discovery, but require immutable SecretVersion IDs for executable/approved bindings; latest may exist only in an explicit rotation proposal. Add provider/tenant/type constraints, complete schema traversal and validated resolution inside execution nodes.
units.responsibilityConflict: latest can resolve to different credential bytes after approval without changing the Connector configuration digest. A valid UUID also proves neither ownership nor that the responsible human may use it.

units.function: Unit tests recursively replacing registered plaintext secrets across Run comments/context/events/transcripts while stripping internal redaction registry material and preserving Date instances.
units.dependencyDirection: Arbitrary Run projection values and an exact plaintext registry enter a recursive sanitizer before API/log presentation; REDACTED_EVENT_VALUE replaces matches.
units.keyDataModels: Registered secret strings, comment/heartbeat/wake/context/stdout/event/log fields, internal redaction material and Date values.
units.lifecycle: Exact substrings are replaced everywhere, longer overlapping secrets are processed first, registry material is removed from context and Date objects retain type even when no secrets are registered.
units.testAssessment: Broad projection fields, overlap ordering and Date regressions are covered. Missing are cycles, Error/Map/Set/Buffer/typed arrays, encoded/base64/URL/split-stream variants, minimum secret length/false positives, huge payload performance, secret rotation registry completeness and proof sanitization precedes persistence, realtime events and every export sink.
units.designRationale: Contain credentials accidentally echoed by Agents or tools without corrupting normal structured Run timestamps.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must prevent secrets and protected data from leaving execution nodes while preserving trustworthy evidence completeness metadata.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT exact-value redaction as a final defense, not the primary boundary. Resolve secrets only in execution nodes, stream-scan/redact before persistence or egress, classify truncation/redaction in evidence, use data-loss prevention rules and preserve protected originals only under separate encrypted access policy.
units.responsibilityConflict: Post-hoc replacement cannot undo a secret already sent to a model/tool or external sink, and a redacted transcript is not complete evidence unless the record identifies what class was removed, by which policy and where an authorized original resides.
